verdicts.scope: only calligraphy.json sections[3].body[1] (الْأَرْقَام الْعَرَبِيَّة) and coffee.json sections[1].titleAr (الْقَهْوَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّة); keep 'Arabic (the language)' wherever the word stands alone as the language
verdicts.reason: In both phrases الْعَرَبِيَّة is an attributive adjective agreeing with a feminine/non-human-plural noun (export l.149, l.356); 'the language' is wrong there. The coffee titleSegs already say 'Arabic · adj'.
يَسْكُنُ أَكْثَرُ الْبَدْوِ: أَكْثَرُ + definite plural in idāfa = 'most of'. Tap 'more' (l.903) contradicts the line's own English.
اِبْنُهُ الْأَكْبَر = his eldest son; the English of the same line says 'eldest' and the reading segs say 'the eldest'. Tap 'the biggest' (l.1162) is misleading.

verdicts.scope: food.json words[9].segs (source seg) and the taps of مَرِيئًا in sections[3].body[1] and quiz[3].options[1]; the word only occurs in this fixed phrase, so changing its gloss is safe
verdicts.reason: Real error: there is no وَ in هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا, so 'and may it be wholesome' invents a clitic. The reviewer's 'wholesome, may it be wholesome' is redundant; simply dropping 'and' is the minimal correct fix.

verdicts.reason: Tap at l.1476 shows 'more; more; the most', a merge duplicate; in كُلْ أَكْثَر ('eat more') only 'more' fits.

verdicts.reason: l.1630 and l.1636 show 'the Treasury; the Treasury (famous building in Petra)': a two-reading merge repeating one sense.

يَا أُسْتَاذُ سَامِي is the fully vocalised form, but the unmarked يَا أُسْتَاذ is not a wrong vowel: it is the course's consistent house style for vocatives. A scan of content/ finds يَا أُسْتَاذ about 85 times (including يَا أُسْتَاذ كَرِيم ×6, يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود, يَا سَيِّدَة سَمِيرَة, يَا دُكْتُورَة فَاطِمَة, يَا عَمّ حَسَن), all without ḍamma. Changing this one line would make it the only exception and teach an inconsistency; it does not change the word or teach a wrong case. If the owner wants munādā ḍamma, it must be a course-wide decision, not a one-line fix.

verdicts.fix: Engine: hyphen after every clitic glossed as clitic + word (bi-khayr, bi-qalamin, wa-bi-ḥibrin, bi-khaṭṭi, wa-bāridatun, bi-thamāniyati, li-fustānin …) and, for a name behind a clitic, lower-case clitic + capitalised name: wa-Bākistāna (sentence-initial capital applies to the first word only, not to a mid-sentence clitic).
verdicts.scope: engine (tap.ts cliticReading / nameReading); no content change
verdicts.reason: Confirmed: l.49 'fī Īrāna Wabākistāna' (capital on the clitic, name lower case, no hyphen, mid-sentence) and the solid/hyphenated mix in the same texts. Same root cause as days-21-30 #1.

verdicts.fix: Engine: capitalise every token whose seg is marked as a name in every inflected form (bintu Karīm, Ismuhu Karīm al-Miṣrī, Abī smuhu Karīm, fī Miṣr, Fī Ramaḍān, fī l-Qāhirati, Al-Khazna); keep karīm lower case only where its seg means 'generous' (Ramaḍān karīm).
verdicts.reason: Confirmed: l.1033 'Anā Laylā, bintu karīm' while the seg is 'Karim (first name) · name'; l.1611 'fī miṣr', l.1639 'Al-khazna' vs l.1646 'l-Khaznata'. A learner reads bintu karīm as 'daughter of a generous man'.

summary: 10 findings checked against audit/culture.txt, the culture JSON and tap.ts. AGREE 8 / CHANGE 1 / DISAGREE 1. All gloss findings are real and must stay scoped to their lines (except the deduplicated الْخَزْنَة and مَرِيئًا glosses, which are single-sense words). #4 changed to the minimal 'may it be wholesome'. #8 (يَا أُسْتَاذ سَامِي) rejected: the unmarked vocative is the course's consistent house style (~85 occurrences), not a wrong form.
